message.content:
Can you help me draft a power of attorney document tailored to my needs?

Yes — I can help you draft a power of attorney tailored to your needs. Below is a clear, step-by-step example that explains what a power of attorney is, asks the right questions to determine the appropriate type, and provides a sample template you can adapt. This example assumes you want a durable general power of attorney for financial matters; if you need a different type (medical, limited, springing, etc.), the same process applies with different content.

1) Explanation and purpose
A power of attorney (POA) is a legal document by which one person (the principal) grants another (the agent or attorney-in-fact) authority to act on the principal’s behalf. A durable POA remains effective if the principal becomes incapacitated; a general POA gives broad authority over financial and legal matters; a limited POA grants only specific powers for a limited time or purpose.

2) Key decisions to make
- Type: durable general POA, limited POA, medical/healthcare POA, or springing POA.
- Agent: who you trust to act for you.
- Successor agent: who will act if the first agent can’t.
- Effective date: immediately upon signing, or only upon incapacity (springing).
- Scope: specific powers to grant or exclude (banking, real estate, tax filings, gifts, etc.).
- Duration and termination conditions.
- State-specific formalities: witnessing and notarization requirements.

3) Questions to determine content
- Who will be the agent and any successor agents (names, addresses)?
- Do you want the POA to be durable if you become incapacitated?
- Do you want the agent to have broad authority or only specific powers (list them)?
- Should the agent be allowed to make gifts, handle retirement accounts, or transfer real estate?
- When should the POA become effective?
- Are there any special limitations or instructions for the agent?

4) Sample durable general power of attorney (adapt to local law)
[Begin sample — adapt to your jurisdiction and have an attorney review]

POWERS OF ATTORNEY

I, [Principal Name], residing at [Address], hereby appoint [Agent Name], residing at [Agent Address], as my Attorney-in-Fact to act for me in all matters as fully as I could do if personally present.

1. Effective Date and Durability
This Power of Attorney shall become effective immediately upon execution and shall not be affected by my subsequent incapacity or disability.

2. Grant of General Authority
I grant my Attorney-in-Fact full power and authority to manage and conduct all of my affairs, including but not limited to:
- Real property transactions;
- Banking and financial transactions;
- Management of personal and business property;
- Tax matters and claims;
- Insurance transactions;
- Retirement plan transactions;
- Litigation and legal matters;
- Personal and family maintenance.

3. Specific Powers (examples — include as needed)
- To access safe deposit boxes and sign any documents required;
- To sign and file tax returns and represent me before tax authorities;
- To sell, mortgage, lease, or convey real property on my behalf;
- To make gifts in accordance with [specify limits or policies];

4. Limitations
The Attorney-in-Fact shall not: [list any specific prohibitions, e.g., make gifts beyond $X, disinherit specific beneficiaries, or change beneficiary designations unless expressly allowed].

5. Successor Agents
If [Agent Name] is unable or unwilling to serve, I appoint [Successor Agent Name] as successor Attorney-in-Fact.

6. Liability and Compensation
The Attorney-in-Fact shall act in my best interest and may be reimbursed for reasonable expenses. The Attorney-in-Fact shall not be liable for decisions made in good faith.

7. Revocation
This Power of Attorney may be revoked by me in writing at any time, subject to any actions already taken by the Attorney-in-Fact.

8. Governing Law
This document is governed by the laws of the State of [State].

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have executed this Durable Power of Attorney on this ___ day of __________, 20__.

Principal: _____________________________
[Printed Name]

Witnesses:
1. ______________________
2. ______________________

Notary Acknowledgment
[Notary block as required by your jurisdiction]

[End sample]

5) How to adapt and finalize
- Replace bracketed placeholders with actual names and addresses.
- Add or remove powers according to your preferences.
- Add specific instructions or limitations for the agent.
- Make sure to follow witnessing and notarization rules in your state.
- Consider having an attorney review the final document to ensure enforceability.

If you want, tell me:
- Which state or country the POA will be used in,
- The type of authority you want (financial, medical, limited, durable, springing),
- The name(s) of the agent and successor agent, and any specific powers or limits you want included,

and I’ll draft a version tailored to those details.
